d: Choir of Schiavi, Rome. Rome, on a trophy of remains surrounded by several Schiavi, after hearing the praises of the serene Prince Alexander Charles of Poland, the common jubilation for the coming of St. highness, resolves to represent the cases of St. Alexis, which among his citizens was no less conspiracy in the glory of holiness, than that which were many in the value of arms. And to mention, as she esteemed more than any other dominion the being queen of hearts, she orders that the same Schiavi remain free from the chains.

Eufemiano, Adrasto. Eufemiano, Roman senator and father of St. Alessio, met with Adrasto, a Roman knight, who came again from the war, rejoices at his return; and as he entered to discuss the cases of Alessio, he took the opportunity to tell him about the departure of him followed many years before; and while he is indicted of such adversity, he is with particular affection compassionate and consoled by Adrasto.
S. Alessio.
S. Alessio, Marzio, Curzio.

Demon Choir inside the scene. Another Choir, dancing. Picked up the Devil by the hellish choirs, who promise great victory, make joy with dances he puts himself to the task of tempting and seducing the constancy of the Saint. He changes the scene into a hell and in the distance they represent the pains of the damned. He sings the air that follows, and from a choir of Demons he is accompanied with different mutants.

Mother, Bride, Nanny, Martius, Curzio. The Mother and the Bride of St. Alexis mourn the absence of him, consoled in vain by the Nanny, for advice of which they turn to pray god, so that he prospers wherever he is.

Added by introduction of a dance. Moved Curzio to diporto to the villas of his Master, he is thinking of preparing some hold-ups, then to use it as a ridicule of the Pilgrim; the plan to lead you the Rustici of those woods offers the occasion of a pleasant dance. The scene is changed into a forest.
Euphemian, with the consolation of the relatives of Adrastus in his return, weeps his unhappiness, to be almost hopeless to see his son again.
The devil points out that he has planned a plot for which he hopes that the saint will be forced to discover himself and return to the delights of the century.

Bride in pilgrim's dress. Nurse. The Bride, determined to go looking for the world the lost Alessio, appears in pilgrim's dress, and while she speaks of such thought, is observed by the Nurse, who without discovering herself to her, brings her warning to the Mother.

Mother, Bride, Nurse, S. Alessio, Marzio and Curzio. Try to prevent the Mother from preventing the design of the Bride: indeed, stimulated by the example of a great love, she resolves to imitate her, and to leave with her. St. Alessio, understood this novelty, recommended first to the divine help, tries with various reasons to consider her from the intended path. The Bride, placed in much ambiguity, and renewing herself more than ever the pain for the absence of her husband, is less.
S. Alessio. S. Alessio for the miserable labor of relatives, agitated by different thoughts, considers himself if he should manifest himself.

St. Alessio, Devil, in the form of Hermit. In this variety of thoughts he is met by the Devil, who under the habit of old Hermit procures with several reasons to induce the Saint to discover himself to 'kins. However, he being more confused than persuaded, does not let doubt that it is an illusion of hell, in order to ask God that in so much need you do not abandon him.

Angelo, S. AlessioApparendo a Angelo, assures him that the Hermit was the Devil, and that the reasons that he put forward must be despised by S. Alessio, who with particular inspiration is called by God on a rather admirable, imitable path. He reveals to him the near death and the greatness of the prize prepared for him in heaven. And the exhortation to wait for that passage with fearless soul. From which comforted, the Saint invites death, and is meditating on the tranquility that the righteous find in it. The Angel comes flying from heaven.

Devil and Martius. The Devil returns, determined to make every effort to overcome Alessio in the short space that remains of his life. He came over from Marzio who, believing him a Hermit and wanting to mock him as he used to do with Alessio enters seco in discourse. Admired with him, he causes to hold him, but he comes in several ways ridiculed by the Devil.

Religion. Religion appears in order to witness the devoted transit of Alessio, and, boasting of the work of him now reached the prize deserved, invites the world to pursue virtue. Religion passes through the air in a cart surrounded by clouds.

Euphemian, Adrasto, Nunzio. While Euphemian is grieving for his misfortunes in the company of Adrasto, he hears a warning, as in the major church a voice from heaven had been heard calling to the stars the troubled soul in the world. Therefore, rejoiced, he gathers that it too could console himself once with the return of his son; and that for any misery one must never lose hope.
Demon, and choir of Demons. The devil, having in vain used every work against the Saint, full of confusion plunges into hell.

Adrasto, Chorus, NunzioAdrasto, for having seen several people walk to the house of Euphemian goes in company with others to certify their reason and, meeting in one of the same house, hears from him the death, the reconnaissance of St. Alexius, and from the same is introduced into the room where his body lies.

Euphemian, Bride, Mother, Martius, Curzio, Adrasto and Choir of Angels inside the scene. Parents bitterly weep the death of Alessio. We read the letter written by him before dying. Changing the scene, the loggias and the garden of the palace appear, in which, under the stairs, lies the body of the Saint.

Choir of Angels, inside the scene. Euphemian, Mother, Bride. Angels, accompanying the soul of the Holy, persuade relatives, who wrongly, are woeful in the world for the death of those who are received in heaven with so much joy.

Religion, Choir of Virtues, Choir of Angels. Religion appears from the house of the Holy and secus comes a choir of Virtues figured for the eight Beatitudes, which were means to Alessio to get the glory. Religion rejoices at the purchase made by heaven in St. Alessio assigns to him the temple, which from the ancient Romans was dedicated to Hercules. Then the Religion left, going on to consecrate the temple to St. Alessio and while the Angels continue the songs, they celebrate the Virtues with dances.
